newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus says Korean Air buys four A330s.
newsitem.headline: Airbus says Korean Air buys four A330s.

text.p: Korean Air has signed a contract to buy four Airbus A330 passenger jets, bringing its total orders of A330s to 13, Airbus Industrie said on Thursday.
The four new planes will be delivered in 1998 and 1999 which will allow all the A330s on order to enter service between now and 2000, the European aircraft consortium said in a statement.

The latest orders, which are for either the A330-200 or A330-300 versions, will be powered by variants of the PRatt & Whitney PW4000 engine family. Pratt & Whitney is a unit of United Technologies Corp.
The Korean airline also holds options for six A330s, making it one of the largest customers for this aircraft type, Airbus said.
Average list price for an A330-300 is around $125 million, industry sources said. The A330 seats 335 passangers in two classes.

Airbus Industrie is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
